description: We are Levi Squad, building AstraGuard AI, an offline-first health monitoring system for astronauts on Moon and Mars missions. Our skills: web development, Python/FastAPI, PostgreSQL and machine learning. We're looking for people in UI/UX design, ML/data science, biomedical knowledge or pitch storytelling. All levels welcome!
summary:
Team Levi Squad developed AstroPulse / CrewCheck, an offline-first astronaut health decision-support web application for deep-space missions.

It bridges the gap between daily astronaut vitals and clinical standards by comparing metrics against personal 14-day rolling baselines.

Built-in safeguards feature a 24-hour data-quality guard to eliminate false logging spikes and a smart 4-tier alert escalation system.

The system integrates official NASA datasets (OSDR OSD-575, HRP Evidence, and HRR Risks) alongside the Framingham Heart Study dataset.

Technologies utilized include HTML5, Vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, and Chart.js to ensure robust, standalone offline operations.
details:
• Project Title: AstroPulse / CrewCheck (developed by Team Levi Squad for NASA Space Apps Challenge #05).
  • Core Mission: An offline-first astronaut health decision-support web application tailored for deep-space and resource-constrained missions.
  • Personalized Baselines: Compares daily astronaut physiological vitals directly against individual 14-day rolling personal baselines rather than static population averages.
  • Data-Quality Guard: Features an advanced 24-hour data-quality guard to prevent erroneous logging spikes or missing inputs from triggering false alarms.
  • Alert System: Incorporates a smart 4-tier alert escalation system that categorizes physiological shifts from nominal status to critical warning levels.
  • Interactive Modules: Includes built-in interactive health-learning modules designed for autonomous astronaut self-care and medical guidance.
  • NASA Data Integration: Integrates official NASA datasets and repositories, including OSDR Study OSD-575 and Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports.
  • Clinical Risk Mapping: Backed by NASA Human Research Roadmap (HRR) risk guidelines covering cardiovascular adaptations, decompression sickness, and sleep/circadian desynchronization.
  • Public Health Benchmarks: Cross-references public health metrics using the Framingham Heart Study dataset from Kaggle for comprehensive physiological tracking.
  • Tech Stack: Built using lightweight, resilient web technologies including HTML5, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6), Tailwind CSS, and Chart.js for seamless offline execution.
